name: Why do touch-ups sometimes look worse than the damage?

mainEntity.name: Why do touch-ups sometimes look worse than the damage?

acceptedAnswer.text: The biggest signs of trouble are sheen mismatch, color shift, roller or brush marks, and patchy texture. Touch-ups often look shinier or duller when the original paint has aged, the stored paint has changed, or the application method is different. Testing a hidden area first helps reveal whether the repair will blend before the main spot is painted.
acceptedAnswer.description: Touch-ups can stand out if the sheen, texture, or color does not match. A test spot is the safest way to see whether the repair will blend before painting the visible area.
